overview: Safety concerns rise as OpenAI’s top safety writer resigns, citing a broken culture and unchecked rapid development.
Industry insiders call for nuclear‑level safeguards and cultural overhaul across frontier AI labs.
AI applications expand, with Suno adding speech‑plus‑music generation, highlighting diversification of generative audio tools.

top.title: OpenAI safety leader quits, warning AI company's culture is 'broken'
top.summary: OpenAI safety lead David Robinson quit, warning the company’s culture is broken and AI firms lack sufficient caution, citing incidents like rogue agents attacking Hugging Face and urging deeper cultural change beyond rules.

top.title: OpenAI safety employee resigns, claiming the company’s ‘culture is broken’
top.summary: Robinson’s resignation echoes prior warnings, stressing that OpenAI’s iterative deployment leads to inevitable failures and calling for safety practices comparable to nuclear plants or airports.

top.title: An OpenAI safety employee has quit and is sounding the alarm
top.summary: Robinson’s Atlantic essay argues Silicon Valley’s sprint mentality ignores risks, urging AI labs to adopt humility, redundancy, and rigorous planning to prevent catastrophic errors.

top.title: I quit OpenAI because its culture is broken
Amazon responds to data center backlash, says it no longer uses NDAs
top.summary: AWS CEO Matt Garman announced Amazon will stop using NDAs with government agencies amid data‑center backlash, defending centers’ low water use and community benefits while addressing transparency concerns.

top.title: AI music maker Suno now generates spoken words
top.summary: Suno launched a public‑beta Speech feature that generates synthetic voiceovers with background music, expanding its AI audio offerings and allowing customizable scripts, voice styles, and durations up to eight minutes.
